meta.title: Industries we supply
meta.description: Fasteners for construction sites, manufacturing floors, automotive shops, electrical panels, infrastructure plant, and machinery stores.

hero.title: Every sector runs on the same sizes — packed the way stores issue them.
hero.lede: From formwork nails to machine-frame bolts, we supply matched lots for contractors, OEMs, and maintenance stores who refill the same bin every month.
hero.imageAlt: Industrial fasteners used across construction and manufacturing

overview.title: Six sectors. One packing standard.
overview.lede: Each industry gets grade-marked fasteners counted and labelled — not a mixed handful from three mills.

items.title: Site to plant
items.body: Construction, infrastructure, and machinery stores share the same metric sizes — M8 to M24 bolts, wire nails, anchor sets.

items.title: Shop-floor ready
items.body: Manufacturing and automotive lines get prevailing-torque nuts and machine screws that still undo after a year of vibration.

items.title: Panel and plant
items.body: Electrical cabinets and outdoor frames receive pan-head screws and galvanized hex sets sized for the drawing, not leftover tins.

grid.title: Where our fasteners land — and what they hold together.
grid.lede: Open a sector for typical uses, what we supply, and what to send for a quote.

detail.requirementsLabel: What to send for a quote
detail.quoteBody: Diameter, length, grade, finish, and quantity are enough. We will return a counted lot — not a mixed handful.
detail.relatedLede: Other sectors that refill the same metric sizes from our four product lines.

construction.body: Contractors order wire nails by kilogram, concrete nails by length, and foundation bolts by diameter — not by a machine drawing. We pack each lot counted and labelled so a site crate can be issued straight to formwork, masonry, or steel fixers.
highlights: Wire nails in kg bags — 1", 1.5", 2", 2.5", 3" and custom lengths
Concrete nails for masonry battens and shuttering plates
Foundation anchor bolts M12 to M24 with matching nuts and washers
Hex bolts for site steel connections — plain or galvanized finish
requirements: Nail length or bolt diameter and length
Finish — plain, zinc, or hot-dip galvanized
Quantity by count, kg, or set
Site location if outdoor exposure matters

industrial-manufacturing.body: Machine builders need grade-marked bolts and prevailing-torque nuts that still undo after a year on the line. We gauge bolts and nuts as matched pairs so a guard rail or conveyor joint does not mix two mills on one connection.
highlights: Hex bolts 8.8 and 10.9 with grade-marked heads
Nyloc and prevailing-torque lock nuts in matched thread gauges
M6 to M20 sets for machine frames and guard assemblies
Stainless sets where wash-down or chemical exposure applies
requirements: Diameter, length, and grade (8.8, 10.9, A2, A4)
Nut type — full, nyloc, or flange
Quantity per assembly or monthly refill volume
Drawing reference if a non-standard length applies

automotive.body: Body shops and fixture builders cannot have a joint walk off under vibration. We supply machine screws and lock nuts in the sizes a service kit or jig already uses — packed so a stores bin can be refilled without a new part number.
highlights: Machine screws M4 to M8 in pan, CSK, and hex head
Prevailing-torque nuts for fixtures and service kits
Metric sets for jig plates and body-hold hardware
Counted bags sized for monthly shop-floor refills
requirements: Screw diameter, length, and head type
Lock-nut specification if vibration-critical
Kit quantity or monthly usage estimate
Finish requirement — plain, zinc, or black oxide

electrical.body: Panel shops should not mix leftover hardware from three tins. We supply M3 to M6 machine screws in pan and CSK so PLC cabinets, junction boxes, and nameplates get a consistent lot every reorder.
highlights: Pan-head and CSK machine screws M3 to M6
Thread lengths matched to standard panel thicknesses
Stainless screws for outdoor or humid enclosures
Counted sets for recurring panel SKUs
requirements: Screw size, length, and head style
Panel material and thickness if unsure on length
Stainless grade if specified (A2 or A4)
Monthly volume or per-SKU count

infrastructure.body: Pump bases, shed columns, and utility frames sit outdoors through monsoon season. Hot-dip or zinc hex sets and anchor bolts leave our bay marked and counted — rust on the first rain is not acceptable on a base plate joint.
highlights: Anchor bolt sets with template-ready lengths
Hot-dip galvanized hex bolts and nuts M16 to M24
Full sets — bolt, nut, and washer gauged together
Foundation and column bases for outdoor plant
requirements: Anchor diameter, embedment length, and projection
Galvanizing specification — zinc or hot-dip
Base plate thickness and hole pattern if known
Project quantity and dispatch schedule

machinery.body: OEM kitting and MRO stores need standard metric sizes held as stock items — not one-off specials every reorder. We pack bolts and nuts in the sizes a drawing already calls out so a sub-assembly bin refills without a new part number.
highlights: Standard metric hex bolts and nuts M6 to M24
OEM kit sets packed by assembly reference
MRO refill bins in counted bags or kg lots
Grade-marked lots for traceable sub-assembly builds
requirements: Part list or drawing reference
Diameter, length, grade, and finish per line item
Kit quantity or bin refill cycle
Matched bolt-and-nut pairs where required

support.title: From enquiry to your site
support.lede: Four clear steps — from your size list to a counted lot leaving our Gandhinagar bay.

steps.title: Send the size list
steps.body: Diameter, length, grade, finish, and quantity — or a drawing reference. That is enough to return a rate.
steps.imageAlt: Assorted fasteners sorted by size for a packing list enquiry

steps.title: Matched as pairs
steps.body: Bolts and nuts are gauged together. Grade is marked on the head so a store bin does not mix two mills on one joint.
steps.imageAlt: Hex bolt and matching nut gauged as a pair with grade on the head

steps.title: Counted before dispatch
steps.body: Every bag and crate is counted in Gandhinagar. The packing list must match the lot before it is sealed.
steps.imageAlt: Workers counting and labelling fastener bags in the packing bay

steps.title: Depart from our bay
steps.body: Labelled crates leave Gandhinagar for your site, shop, or plant — the same counted lot, ready to issue on arrival.
steps.imageAlt: Packed fastener crates leaving the Hakimi Industries workshop bay

cta.title: Tell us the sector and the sizes you refill.
cta.body: Name, phone, and a short note are enough. We will call you back with a counted lot — not a catalogue essay.
